extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and patent applicants (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for correcting inventorship in issued patents (35 U.S.C. 256 / 37 CFR 1.324) and for claiming or restoring benefit/priority under 35 U.S.C. 119/120 (37 CFR 1.78). Covers required statements, fees, forms, timing, petitions, motions in contested proceedings, and double-patenting/ownership considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent validity when inventorship error correctable
rubrics_metrics.description: The error of omitting inventors or naming persons who are not inventors shall not invalidate the patent in which such error occurred if it can be corrected as provided in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court before which such matter is called in question may order correction of the patent on notice and hearing of all parties concerned and the Director shall issue a certificate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to issue certificate correcting inventorship (37 CFR 1.324(a) / 35 U.S.C. 256)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever through error a person is named in an issued patent as the inventor, or an inventor is not named in an issued patent, the Director, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 256, may, on application of all the parties and assignees, or on order of a court before which such matter is called in question, issue a certificate naming only the actual inventor or inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to correct inventorship of a patent involved in an interference must comply with this section and be accompanied by appropriate motions under § 41.121(a)(2) or (a)(3) as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑September 16, 2012 petition contents for correcting inventorship (37 CFR 1.324(b) post‑2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed on or after September 16, 2012 to correct inventorship in a patent must be accompanied by: (1) a statement from each person who is being added as an inventor and each person who is currently named as an inventor either agreeing to the change of inventorship or stating that he or she has no disagreement; (2) a statement from the assignee(s) of the parties submitting a statement under (1) agreeing to the change of inventorship (must comply with 37 CFR 3.73(c)); and (3) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition filed on or after September 16, 2012 lacks any of these items the petition is dismissed (use form paragraph 10.16.01). Each entity having an ownership interest must provide a statement. See MPEP references for form and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA petition contents for correcting inventorship (pre‑Sept 16, 2012 37 CFR 1.324(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed before September 16, 2012 must be accompanied by: (1) where one or more persons are being added, a statement from each person being added that the inventorship error occurred without any deceptive intention on his or her part; (2) a statement from current named inventors (including any inventor being deleted) either agreeing to the change or stating no disagreement; (3) a statement from all assignees of the parties submitting statements under (1) and (2) agreeing to the change of inventorship and complying with 37 CFR 3.73(b); and (4) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An example sufficient statement is provided (explicit wording that the error occurred without deceptive intention). The examiner will check only for the required language and will not adjudicate whether deceptive intention actually existed (see MPEP § 2012). Petitions missing required items should be dismissed (form paragraph 10.16.fti) or denied if insubstantial items are insufficient (form paragraph 10.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee/ownership statements requirement (37 CFR 3.73(b)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement is required from all assignees of the parties submitting inventor statements agreeing to the change of inventorship; the assignee statement must comply with 37 CFR 3.73(b) (pre‑AIA) or 3.73(c) (post‑AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entity having an ownership interest in the patent must provide such a statement. The assignee statement agreeing to the change must be accompanied by a proper statement establishing ownership unless such a statement is already of record. See MPEP § 324 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and fee requirements (forms, certificates, and fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must include required fee(s) set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(b) (petition fee) and appropriate forms (e.g., form PTO/SB/44, certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting the Office to effectuate a court order correcting inventorship pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 256, submit a copy of the court order and a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 to the Certificates of Correction Branch and file PTO/SB/44. Use prescribed form paragraphs (10.13–10.18) and prepare certificates using form paragraph 10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when inventor unavailable or refuses to sign
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is not available, or refuses, to submit a required statement, the assignee may consider filing a reissue application to correct inventorship because the inventor's statement is not required for a non‑broadening reissue application to correct inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1412.04 for reissue practice and strategic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contested proceedings / motions format for inventorship correction
rubrics_metrics.description: In an interference under 37 CFR part 41, subpart D, a request for correction of inventorship in a patent must be in the form of a motion under § 41.121(a)(2) (or (a)(3) pre‑AIA). In a contested case under part 42, subpart D, a request must be in the form of a motion under § 42.22. Motions must comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions under § 41.121(a)(2)/(a)(3) or § 42.22 must include the same statements and fees required by 37 CFR 1.324 and follow Board practice for contested proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition standards for petitions to correct inventorship (grant/dismiss/deny/waiver requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: If required items are missing the petition should be dismissed; if missing items are insufficient, the petition should be denied. Requests for waiver under 37 CFR 1.183 of requirements that are statutory will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph for grant (10.13/10.14), dismissal (10.16/10.16.01), or denial (10.17). If the deficiency is curable, dismissal with opportunity to renew is appropriate. Petitions requesting waiver of requirements of 37 CFR 1.324 that are statutory (35 U.S.C. 256) must be dismissed (form paragraph 10.18). Petitions requesting waiver of non‑statutory regulatory requirements may be forwarded to petitions attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example sufficient language for absence of deceptive intention (pre‑AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sufficient statement to satisfy the pre‑AIA requirement: 'The inventorship error of failing to include John Smith as an inventor of the patent occurred without any deceptive intention on the part of John Smith.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing more is required; the examiner will determine only whether the statement contains the required language and will not make any comment as to whether it appears that there was in fact deceptive intention (see MPEP § 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming benefit of provisional applications (37 CFR 1.78(a) timing and reference requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application (other than design) or an international application designating the United States may claim the benefit of one or more prior‑filed provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) if: (i) the later application is filed not later than 12 months after the provisional (subject to paragraph (b)); (ii) each prior provisional names an inventor named in the later application and meets filing/date/fee requirements; and (iii) the later application contains or is amended to contain a reference to each such provisional application, identifying it by provisional application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later‑filed application is a nonprovisional application, the reference must be included in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(5)). Failure to timely submit the reference during pendency (and the specific timing rules in (a)(4)) is considered a waiver of any benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), except as provided in paragraph (c) for unintentional delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for submitting references to earlier filings (37 CFR 1.78(a)(4) & (d)(2)/(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference to the prior‑filed provisional or prior nonprovisional must be submitted during the pendency of the later‑filed application. If the later application is a 111(a) application, the reference also must be submitted within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the later application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior application. For national stage entries, parallel timing rules apply (four months from national stage commencement or sixteen months from the prior filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided (certain grandfathered cases), failure to timely submit the required reference is considered a waiver of the benefit. For applications filed before specific dates, an alternative location for the reference (first sentences of the specification) may suffice (see paragraph (h)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non‑English prior provisional (37 CFR 1.78(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior‑filed provisional was filed in a language other than English and neither an English translation nor a statement that the translation is accurate were previously filed in the prior provisional, the applicant will be notified and given time to file the translation and the statement in the prior provisional. If notice is mailed in a pending nonprovisional, a timely reply must include confirmation that translation/statement were filed in the provisional or the applicant must eliminate the reference in the ADS, or the nonprovisional will be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation and statement may be filed in the provisional application, even if the provisional has become abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of provisional benefit for delayed filing (PCT Rule 26 bis.3 / petition) (37 CFR 1.78(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subsequent nonprovisional is filed after the 12‑month period but within two months thereafter, the benefit of the provisional may be restored under PCT Rule 26 bis.3 (for international applications) or upon petition if the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to restore (filed on or after May 13, 2015) must be filed in the subsequent application and include: (i) the reference to the provisional in an ADS (unless previously submitted); (ii) the petition fee under § 1.17(m); and (iii) a statement that the delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information where there is doubt about unintentionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of unintentionally delayed benefit claims (37 CFR 1.78(c) & (e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is presented after the time period provided, a claim for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (or 120/121/etc.) may be accepted if the reference was unintentionally delayed. A petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim must be accompanied by specified items and a statement that the entire delay was unintentional; the Director may request additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 119(e) delayed claims include the reference and a statement the entire delay was unintentional; for 120/121/etc. delayed claims the petition must include: (1) the required reference unless previously submitted; (2) the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)); and (3) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. Director may require more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) (37 CFR 1.78(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each prior‑filed application must name the inventor or joint inventor named in the later application and must be either (i) an international application entitled to a filing date in accordance with PCT Article 11 and designating the U.S.; (ii) an international design application entitled to a filing date under § 1.1023 and designating the U.S.; or (iii) a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) entitled to a filing date as set forth in § 1.53(b) or (d) with the basic filing fee paid within pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to prior‑filed applications must be included (ADS for nonprovisionals) and must identify the relationship (continuation, divisional, continuation‑in‑part). Failure to timely submit required references is considered a waiver except as provided for unintentional delay; a request for a continued prosecution application under § 1.53(d) serves as the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including cross‑references for which benefit is not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross‑references to other related applications may be made when appropriate, but cross‑references to applications for which a benefit is not claimed under title 35 must not be included in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ADS for benefit references; do not clutter ADS with unrelated cross‑references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications with patentably indistinct claims — elimination and double patenting (37 CFR 1.78(f)/(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant or assignee contain patentably indistinct claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required in the absence of good and sufficient reason for their retention. If an application or a patent under reexamination and another application naming different inventors are owned by the same person and contain patentably indistinct claims, and there is no record showing common ownership or obligation of assignment at the relevant date, the Office may require a statement concerning common ownership and may require identification of the prior inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if claimed inventions were commonly owned or assigned, patentably indistinct claims may be rejected under the doctrine of double patenting. The Office may request statements to clarify ownership/assignment at the effective filing date or date of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provision for applications filed before September 16, 2012 (presentation of references)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before September 16, 2012, the requirement that specific references be presented in an application data sheet is satisfied if the specific reference is presented in the first sentence(s) of the specification following the title in a nonprovisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before September 16, 2012, or resulting from an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph does not apply to a specific reference submitted for a petition under paragraph (b) to restore the benefit of a provisional application.
